ALVEOLI: A tiny sac for holding air in the lungs; formed by the terminal dilation of tiny air passageways.
APPENDIX: A vestigial process that extends from the lower end of the cecum and that resembles a small pouch.
BACKBONE: The series of vertebrae forming the axis of the skeleton and protecting the spinal cord.
BLADDER: The sac that stores urine before it leaves the body.
BRONCHI: Either of the two main branches of the trachea.
CALCIUM: A mineral, the main element in bones and teeth.
CALF: The fleshy back part of the leg below the knee.
CAPILLARY: Any of the minute blood vessels connecting arterioles with venules.
CAPSULE: A structure that encloses a body part.
CEREBRAL: Of or relating to the cerebrum or brain.
CILIA: Tiny hair-like projections on the surface of some cells, such as those lining the airways.
CORPUSCLE: A blood cell, red or white.
CORTEX: The outer layer of an organ, especially the folded grey matter of the brain.
DIAPHRAGM: A muscular partition separating the abdominal and thoracic cavities; functions in respiration.
DIGIT: A finger or toe in human beings or corresponding body part in other vertebrates.
DILATION: Widening or enlarging, as of the pupils or blood vessels.
DIMPLE: A small natural hollow in the cheek or chin.
DISC: A pad of cartilage between two vertebrae of the spine.
GENETIC: Of or relating to or produced by or being a gene.
HYDRATION: Taking in enough water to keep the body working properly.
IMMUNE: Relating to the condition of immunity.
IMMUNITY: The body's ability to resist an infection or disease.
IRIS: Muscular diaphragm that controls the size of the pupil.
METABOLISM: The chemical processes by which the body turns food into energy and builds tissue.
MITOCHONDRIA: An organelle containing enzymes responsible for producing energy.
MOLE: A small dark raised spot on the skin.
MOTOR: Of nerves or muscles: producing movement.
MOUTH: The opening through which food is taken in and vocalizations emerge.
NAIL: Horny plate covering and protecting part of the dorsal surface of the digits.
OBLIQUES: A diagonally arranged abdominal muscle on either side of the torso.
OXYGEN: The gas the body takes in by breathing, needed by every cell.
OXYGENATED: Of blood: carrying oxygen from the lungs.
PERIPHERAL: Of nerves or vessels: lying away from the centre of the body.
PHARYNX: The cavity behind the nose and mouth that leads to the oesophagus and windpipe.
PHLEGM: Expectorated matter; saliva mixed with discharges from the respiratory passages.
PIGMENT: A substance, such as melanin, that gives skin, hair or eyes their colour.
PORE: Any small opening in the skin or outer surface of an animal.
PORTAL: A short vein that carries blood into the liver.
PROTEIN: A large molecule made of amino acids, a building block of muscle and other tissue.
PULSE: The regular throb of the arteries as the heart pumps blood.
PUPIL: The contractile aperture in the center of the iris of the eye; resembles a large black dot.
SKELETON: The hard structure that provides a frame for the body of an animal.
TEETH: The hard white structures in the jaws used for biting and chewing.
TEMPLE: The flat area on either side of the forehead.
THYMUS: A ductless glandular organ at the base of the neck.
THYROID: A gland in the neck that makes hormones controlling metabolism.
UREA: The main nitrogen-containing waste in urine, made in the liver.
VERTEBRAE: One of the bony segments of the spinal column.
WRINKLE: A crease or fold in the skin.
